questions.question: A continuous loss $X$ is reported only as belonging to the fixed bin $(a,b]$, where $a<b$. Under parameter $\theta$, it has CDF $F_\theta$ and density $f_\theta$. Which likelihood contribution describes the observed report?
Under model parameter $\theta$, a loss $X$ has CDF $F_\theta$ and may have atoms at fixed endpoints $a<b$. Which probability is represented by $F_\theta(b)-F_\theta(a)$?

Under model parameter $\theta$, individual losses are reported as membership in disjoint bins with probabilities $p_j(\theta)$. Their reported bin counts are $n_j$. What sample assumption supports the proportional likelihood $\prod_jp_j(\theta)^{n_j}$?
options: Equal monetary widths for all bins.
Identical observed counts in every bin.
Every loss being equal to its bin midpoint.
Independent losses under the specified model.

questions.question: For fixed grouped counts $n_1,\ldots,n_k$ with total $n$, the multinomial likelihood contains coefficient $n!/\prod_j n_j!$ multiplying the probability factors. Why may this coefficient be omitted when maximising over model parameter $\theta$?
options: It is constant in theta for the fixed reported data.
It is always equal to one.
It is the probability of the observed table by itself.

questions.question: A loss model assigns probabilities 0.2 and 0.5 to two disjoint reported bins. These bins omit part of the population, and sampling is not conditioned on their union. What probability must an outside bin carry?
Four independent losses produce counts 3 and 1 in two exhaustive bins with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, where $0<p<1$. What is the log-likelihood up to a parameter-free constant?

Positive losses are exponential with rate $\lambda>0$, and are reported in bins $(0,100]$ and $(100,\infty)$. The fitted probability of the upper bin is 0.4. Using $\mathbb{P}(X>100)=\mathrm{e}^{-100\lambda}$, what fitted rate is implied?

Under model parameter $\theta$, a grouped-loss likelihood includes a bin with observed count $n_j=0$ and candidate probability $0<p_j(\theta)<1$. What factor does this bin contribute to the probability product?
A parameter candidate assigns probability zero to a bin containing at least one observed loss in an independent grouped sample. What happens to its likelihood?
options: It is unchanged because unobserved exact values are unknown.
It remains positive after replacing the bin by its midpoint.
It becomes positive if the parameter-free coefficient is large enough.
It is zero because an observed event is assigned zero probability.

questions.question: Under model parameter $\theta$, two adjacent reported bins have model probabilities $p_1(\theta),p_2(\theta)$ and counts $n_1,n_2$. They are merged into one reported interval. What is the new probability and recorded count?
A positive loss model assigns probabilities 0.2,0.3,0.5 to bins $(0,10]$, $(10,20]$, $(20,\infty)$. No within-bin law is specified. What is the sharp possible range of its CDF value $F(15)$?

Four losses are uniform on $(0,\theta)$ with $\theta>2$ and reported counts 2,1,1 in bins $(0,1]$, $(1,2]$, $(2,\infty)$. Their probability likelihood is proportional to $(\theta-2)/\theta^4$. Which of candidate values $\theta=3$ and $\theta=4$ is favoured?
options: They tie because the first two intervals have equal widths.
$\theta=4$, because the tail-bin probability alone is larger.

questions.question: Two independent grouped samples use the same exhaustive bins with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, where $0<p<1$. Sample A has counts 1,1; sample B has counts 3,5. What is their pooled likelihood proportional to?

A loss takes value 1/4 with probability $\theta$ and value 3/4 with probability $1-\theta$, where $0<\theta<1$. Ten independent observations are reported only as membership in the sole bin $(0,1]$. What can this grouped sample identify about $\theta$?
options: It identifies $\theta=1/2$ because the bin midpoint is 1/2.
It favours $\theta$ near one because all losses are in the first bin.
Nothing; its likelihood is constant in theta.
It favours $\theta$ near zero because no loss equals the midpoint.

questions.question: Only counts in the fixed reported bins $(0,1]$ and $(1,\infty)$ are retained from positive losses with model CDF $F_\theta$. During optimisation an analyst replaces the boundary 1 by the candidate parameter $\theta$, keeping the reported counts unchanged. Why is this not the original grouped-data likelihood?
options: Model parameters must never appear inside a CDF argument.
The multinomial coefficient must also be raised to theta.
The boundary change is always harmless because counts add to the sample size.
It replaces the observed fixed-bin events by different events.

questions.question: A model is uniform on $(0,\theta)$ with $\theta>2$. Losses are sampled only conditional on belonging to $R=(0,2]$; reported bins $(0,1]$ and $(1,2]$ have counts 2 and 3. What is their conditional-region likelihood proportional to as a function of $\theta$?
